To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reconstruction accuracy of the HiRes prototype was measured to be 0.4 degrees for stereo opening angles greater 10°, and that the reconstruction accuracy is likely to improve only slightly for the HiRes Stage I detector.
the reconstruction accuracy of extensive air showers viewed in coincidence by two widely separated sites is directly proportional to the square of the opening angle between the sites.
we have developed a reconstruction method for extensive cosmic ray air showers observed by the HiRes prototype detector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cosmic ray showers of ultra high energy (UHE), in particular the study of the highest energy showers (the so-called EHE showers).
the study of the highest energy cosmic rays.
the development of the reconstruction techniques that will be required for the full-scale HiRes experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HiRes detector will have the ability to reconstruct the arrival direction of EHE air showers to an accuracy of about 1°.
the HiRes reconstruction method is capable of reconstructing the arrival direction of EAS to within a few tenths of a degree.
the HiRes reconstruction method is capable of providing the necessary accuracy to reconstruct the direction of EAS to within 0.5° for the vast majority of events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the HiRes detector will have the ability to reconstruct the arrival direction of the primary cosmic ray with an accuracy of 0.5° (95% confidence) for the majority of events, and that this is sufficient for the HiRes experiment to achieve the primary goal of the experiment, namely, the measurement of the energy spectrum of cosmic rays above 10 ^{19} eV with an energy resolution of 0.2.
the HiRes Stage I.0 detector should be capable of reconstructing the directions of EAS to an accuracy of 1° for most events.
the reconstruction of EAS events with the HiRes detector is accurate to better than 0.5°.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reconstruction method is robust and can be applied with confidence to the HiRes data.
the HiRes Stage I.0 detector should be capable of determining the arrival directions of EAS with a median error of about 1°.
the HiRes detector will be capable of reconstructing air shower geometries with a median error of less than 1° for most events.
